claim: NPCServices.xml in Root.wad (root class hash 0x32a408e1) holds 41 NPC service definitions as BINd v7 binary records, each with a name, an 8-byte identifier and fixed property fields. It carries registrar data (RegistrarServiceA) and trainer data (WizTrainingServiceA, GardenTrainingServiceA, FishingTrainingServiceA, MonsterMagicTrainingServiceA).
disproof: A Root.wad from the same revision whose NPCServices.xml entry decompresses to fewer or more than 41 ServiceA names, lacks RegistrarServiceA, or shows a different root class hash at bytes 8-11.
evidence: Decompressed entry is 3150 bytes; first 4 bytes are ASCII BINd, bytes 4-7 are u32 7, bytes 8-11 are u32 0x32a408e1.
41 null-terminated names ending in ServiceA follow the 54 7d 83 marker, each preceded by a 1-byte flag.
WizTrainingServiceA is entry 5, GardenTrainingServiceA entry 6, FishingTrainingServiceA entry 7, MonsterMagicTrainingServiceA entry 31 of 41.
Each service record carries an 8-byte identifier after the name (e.g. RegistrarServiceA is followed by f5 ea 59 5c 90 01 00 00) and fixed-size property fields; inter-entry gap is a constant 32 bytes.
how_to_repeat: Take your own copy of Root.wad from your own r806919 install.

Parse the KIWAD v1 index: 13-byte header (magic KIWAD, u32 version, u32 entry count), then per entry 5 little-endian u32s (data offset, uncompressed size, compressed size, checksum, flags), 1 byte, null-terminated name.
Find the NPCServices.xml entry, seek to its data offset, zlib-decompress the entry bytes.
Read bytes 0-3: ASCII BINd. Bytes 4-7: u32 version 7. Bytes 8-11: u32 root class hash 0x32a408e1.
Scan for the 3-byte marker 54 7d 83 followed by 1 flag byte and a null-terminated name ending in ServiceA: 41 matches.
Confirm RegistrarServiceA is present (registrar) and WizTrainingServiceA, GardenTrainingServiceA, FishingTrainingServiceA, MonsterMagicTrainingServiceA are present (trainers).
subject: NPCServices.xml service table under root class hash 0x32a408e1
